questions.prompt: Is there a defect in how this scheduler acquires its locks? If so, mark the line(s) where it is; otherwise answer that there is none.
Two concurrent calls to updateRenditions for different channels arrive while assign(chX, encA) is awaiting store.persistAssignment. What happens?
choices: Both updateRenditions calls wait until the assign call finishes, because the mutex map is shared
Both proceed immediately unless one of them targets chX, which waits for assign to release chX's lock
All three operations are serialized because JavaScript is single-threaded
The updateRenditions calls fail with an error because chX's lock is held

questions.prompt: When the holder of a Mutex calls its release function and there are waiters, what does Mutex.release do?
choices: Sets locked to false and lets all waiters race to set it again
Resolves every waiting promise so they run concurrently
Leaves locked as true and resolves only the oldest waiter, handing ownership directly to it
Throws if the release function is called by a different async context

questions.prompt: assign throws 'encoder encA is full'. What is the state of the locks and data afterwards?
choices: Both locks are released by runExclusive's finally blocks and no assignment was persisted or applied
The encoder lock is released but the channel lock stays held, because the error escapes the outer callback
Both locks stay held until the process restarts
The assignment was persisted to the store but not applied in memory
